headline: Biophysical models link ion channel kinetics, neuronal firing and calcium dynamics
label: Biophysical Excitable Cell Modelling
summary: Recent published work pairs hybrid machine learning and inverse modelling with stochastic and geometric biophysical simulation of excitable cells.
synthesis: The common thread is biophysical modelling of excitable cells in which ionic and geometric mechanisms are represented explicitly and constrained by data. A unified hybrid Hodgkin-Huxley-like model, fitted with non-linear mixed effects to recordings from 20 Kv channel types, outperforms seven prior models. A rat CA1 study links high-frequency stimulation firing bifurcations to electrode-axon geometry and extracellular potassium, while pNMS automates population construction and parallel simulation of neuromuscular cell models via an inverse approach. A deep learning classifier trained on Langevin-simulated data separates eight stochastic intracellular Ca2+ states at 96.8% accuracy. What is new is the pairing of mechanistic models with hybrid machine learning and inverse or population-level calibration. The items do not establish a shared multiscale framework.
